progress.text: Accounting negatives in text: $(1,234), $ (5) and (5)% read as negative numbers when typed, coerced by arithmetic or passed to VALUE, like Excel 365; (-5), ((5)), $5% and dates or times in parentheses stay text
Calc: INDEX(A1:C3,2) (one index on a reference of several rows and columns) is #REF! as in Excel, instead of the whole row; INDEX(A1:C3,2,) still gives the row

Formula hardening: digits too many for a finite number are text, so "1 <400 digits>/<400 digits>" no longer coerces to NaN; a NaN column index in VLOOKUP, HLOOKUP and the D-functions is #VALUE! instead of an index underflow; REGEXREPLACE stops building a result as soon as it can only be too long (a worst case went from 1 GB to 7 MB) (#2163, #2162)

Page Setup paper sizes match Japanese Excel: B4/B5/B6 are the JIS sizes (ISO B4/B5/B6 stay reachable by name), so a Japanese B5 worksheet prints at 182×257 mm; Japanese Postcard (100×148 mm), Double Postcard (148×200 mm), Envelope #3/#4 (120×235/90×205 mm), Kaku #2/#3 (240×332/216×277 mm) and A6 are added, both sizes reach the PDF page (file.exportPdf/file.print MediaBox) and the size survives an XLSX round-trip; the Page Layout Size menu lists them. B4/B5 used to be the ISO sizes, which is changed here

Japanese interface catalog covers every key the Brazilian Portuguese catalog translates: the 398-label shared core plus 545 dialog, message, Backstage and menu strings (943 total, ~43% of ~2,200). A test parses pt.rs's source, so the two catalogs stay in step
Interface translated into Dutch (518 labels: ribbon, context menus, File view, dialog titles, Options); nl, nl-NL, nl-BE locale tags resolve to Dutch

Long flat operator chains (=A1+A2+…) up to Excel's 8,192-character limit (4,096 operands): entering, filling, inserting rows, undo, Evaluate Formula and XLSX save no longer overflow the stack; chains past 64 operands are saved as plain formulas, not dynamic arrays; Spanish formula entry accepts chains past 256 operands (#916)

Linux: "Use system setting" for the theme keeps following the desktop when the XDG Desktop Portal stops answering: each read gives up after 2 s and the next poll reconnects, where one unanswered call stalled the watcher for the rest of the session
Memory: undo steps share a sheet's picture bytes and the workbook's VBA project instead of copying them: 50 edits on a sheet with a 20 MB picture keep 22 MB instead of 992 MB

Memory: floating pictures are decoded at about the size they are drawn, with limits, into a cache bounded by bytes and dropped with their workbook, instead of at full size into one that never let go; two open workbooks no longer show each other's picture. 12 large pictures scrolled through keep 40 MB of textures instead of 258 MB, and none once the workbook closes

The web app keeps its preferences between visits (#1562): theme (dark mode), interface size, language, editing options and the rest of what the desktop app saves in ui.json and prefs.json are kept in the browser's localStorage, written as soon as they change
Memory: the interface and script fallback fonts are read once per run and shared with egui instead of copied into it: an empty workbook settles at 158 MB instead of 258 MB on macOS

Function help follows the interface language: argument hints, autocomplete, Insert Function (search and readable categories) and the Formulas-tab menus read per-language tables of descriptions and argument names; Spanish keeps its 10 functions in the new format

Row auto-fit counts a cell's line breaks only when the cell wraps, as Excel does: a file whose unwrapped cells hold multi-line text no longer opens with tall rows (typing a break still turns wrap on and grows the row)

Lookups (MATCH, XMATCH, VLOOKUP, HLOOKUP, XLOOKUP, LOOKUP) compare numbers exactly like Excel, so a computed key such as =0.1+0.2 no longer finds 0.3; = and COUNTIF/SUMIF keep their 15-digit comparison

Functions: EOMONTH, EDATE, WORKDAY, NETWORKDAYS, YEARFRAC, WEEKNUM, the bond and coupon functions, DISC, BIN2DEC, IM and the other Analysis ToolPak functions give #VALUE! for a reference to more than one cell in a value argument, as Excel 365 does, instead of spilling; array constants and computed arrays still lift

Protect Sheet on a protected sheet: Home › Format, its keytips (HOP, RPS) and the tab menu now read Unprotect Sheet… and unprotect (straight away without a password); a protected sheet that forbids selecting locked (or unlocked) cells is enforced for clicks, arrows and Go To, and the Protect Sheet dialog has the select options (#1346)

XLSX: formulas opened with dynamic-array metadata (cm) keep it on save, with xl/metadata.xml. Before, a formula returning one value lost it (11 of 40 corpus files that have the part lost it entirely), and Excel recalculated some of them with implicit intersection (SUMPRODUCT(IFERROR(...)) changed value)

Recalculation: a dynamic array's anchor given a new formula that reads its old spill area (A1 was =SEQUENCE(3), becomes =SUM(A2:A3)+1 or =SEQUENCE(1,A2+1)) sees that area empty instead of the old values

Recalculation: when two arrays of one recalculation want the same empty cells, the formulas that read the one laid out second (at its anchor or over the cells it would have spilled into) read #SPILL! and empty cells instead of its values

Border keytips: each Alt, H, B letter applies the preset Excel's Borders menu gives it (H,B,O bottom, H,B,B bottom double, H,B,N no border, H,B,A all borders and the rest); they all drew a bottom border before. H,B,M opens Format Cells on the Border tab

Formula-entry Command/Ctrl-click inserts another reference with the locale's argument separator; Shift-click extends from a stable, sheet-aware anchor. Pointer tests cover repeated clicks, reversed ranges, ordinary replacement, typed separators, Spanish syntax, sheet switches and keyboard continuation. Readiness estimates unchanged.

formulas.evaluate (gridcraft-cli eval, MCP evaluateformula) refuses what entering the formula in a cell refuses, with the reason (=SUM(1;2): "expected , or )"), instead of #NAME? for any formula that doesn't parse
Colour menus: Fill Color, Font Color and the Format Cells pickers end with Recent Colors (the last ten custom colours) and More Colors… (hue/saturation area, RGB, hex box, preview, OK/Cancel) (#928)

Multi-level category axes: a category range two or more columns wide beside a column of values (year beside month, Excel's multiLvlStrRef) draws its innermost labels across the plot and the outer levels in rows under them with group separators (columns beside the labels in bar charts), instead of flattening the two columns into twice as many categories; saving writes the reference back as multiLvlStrRef with Excel's level caches, so the axis survives a round trip

Charts: a huge trendline forecast no longer collapses the chart: on a category axis it adds at most four times the data in empty slots (at least 32), the line is sampled over the plot only, and forecasts read from XLSX or set by command are clamped, NaN and infinity becoming 0 (#1148)

XLSX export writes a picture used on several sheets once, as one xl/media part every drawing points to (it wrote a copy per drawing: a 16-sheet workbook with one 112 KB logo grew from 0.4 to 1.9 MB) (#985)

XLSX: [ContentTypes].xml, rels/.rels, the workbook rels and xl/workbook.xml are the first zip entries (document properties last), so libmagic and PHP finfo detect the file type even with large properties (#1090)

Conditional formatting: a rule gathers range statistics only when it reads them (top/bottom, above average, duplicates, scales, bars, icons) and borrows them instead of copying them per cell, so the per-frame lookup of an expression or cell-value rule no longer visits its whole range (#1098, part 1)
Next/previous sheet navigation stops at the first/last visible worksheet instead of activating a hidden boundary sheet; the current selection is retained
Rows auto-fit oversized fonts: opening a file and whole-row/column formatting grow non-custom rows to their tallest font (#833)

Number formats: parsing a format code is linear in its length (long runs of [, , or / no longer take quadratic time), and an unclosed [ is a literal when splitting sections as well as when tokenizing (#810)
Number formats: a fraction denominator with 65,536 zeros no longer crashes; format codes are capped at 255 characters like Excel (longer codes display as General, TEXT gives #VALUE!) (#807)
Security: cell hyperlinks open only http, https and mailto, after a confirmation; other schemes (file:, smb:, UNC, custom handlers) are refused (#777, part 1)
Deleting several Ctrl-selected rows or columns removes them all in one undo step (#758)

XLSX chart sheets are kept on open and save: the sheet, its drawing and chart (with style and colours) are written back unchanged in their place among the worksheets, and left out when the sheet they plot is deleted or renamed or a worksheet took their name (#727)

CSV and tab-separated export is capped at 512 MiB: a sheet whose used range would expand to more (two cells far apart, such as A1 and XFD1048576, are 16 GiB of commas) is refused with the rows, columns and limit, before anything is allocated or written (#528)
PDF writer hardening: text width cannot overflow, all-zero dash arrays and negative or NaN stroke widths are sanitised, non-finite sizes and positions draw nothing (#812)
PDF export writes the document title and author as UTF-16BE when they are not ASCII, so viewers show accents, currency signs and non-Latin text correctly (#813)
TEXT() over a range and chart labels parse each number format code once instead of once per value (#806)
